# Database contract

Migration 017 adds paired immutable diagnostic INITIAL allocation JSON/hash to
`course_plan_request`, freezing the Student allocation command and Course reuse
outcome before assignment. Replay uses identical request/Student identity and
body after a lost allocation response or after storing the path ID; it never
reinterprets INITIAL as REPLAN. Historical allocated diagnostic requests without
this checkpoint fail closed. Rollback refuses to discard checkpoint evidence.
Explicit recoverable resume retains request, path, draft and all checkpoints.
Repeated identical terminal outbox event identities deduplicate transactionally.

PostgreSQL owns Planner configuration and durable job state, not Course or Student state.

- `learning_goal_version` stores immutable published goal versions.
- `learning_target` stores exact target identities inside Learning Planner; it is not a separate Knowledge Tree service.
- `learning_goal_target` maps ordered Course placement metadata to required targets.
- `target_prerequisite` stores directed prerequisite edges.
- `transition_knowledge` stores reviewed source-stack comparisons and analogy boundaries.
- version tables store pedagogy, presentation, and generation policy configuration; published rows are immutable by application policy.
- `planner_policy_activation` selects exact published policy versions for new planning requests without a service rebuild.
- `course_plan_request` stores normalized intent, idempotency, renewable
  lease/retry state, fingerprint metadata, safe shared-course context, a
  successful generated draft for retry, the resulting Course reference, and a
  nullable exact Student-owned `learning_path_id`. `REPLAN` persists the
  caller path at request creation. `INITIAL` checkpoints the ID returned by
  Student immediately after allocation and before later side effects; a retry
  may therefore contain a resolved path even though callers cannot supply one.
  Before any exact-path `REPLAN` or `NO_GAP` PUT, the same row stores an
  all-or-none immutable command checkpoint: kind, expected path version,
  normalized JSON body, SHA-256 semantic hash, checkpoint timestamp, and a
  private planned outcome (`result_code`, optional Course ID, reused flag).
  The hash also binds Student, path, planning-request, Student idempotency
  identities, and that planned outcome. The compare-and-set accepts only an
  empty slot or an identical checkpoint under the active claim. Public
  `result_code`, `course_id`, and `reused` remain unset until Student confirms
  success; transport retry and terminal conflict therefore cannot expose a
  false completed result.
  The claim token must still match whenever its lease is renewed or terminal
  state is committed.
- `planner_outbox` retains immutable schema-v1 rows and stores new terminal `course.plan.completed` and `course.plan.failed` envelopes as schema v2. Request state and its event are one transaction; publication is at least once.
- `practice_learning_route_resolution` stores one immutable idempotency receipt per external task instance. It contains the exact request hash and returned route digest/JSON so retries cannot reinterpret later mastery or policy. The canonical runtime copy of the snapshot belongs to Practice, not this table.
- `teacher_onboarding_plan_handoff` stores the immutable S8 acceptance receipt
  for an exact Student state reference. It retains only canonical UUID audit
  identities, a request hash, and exact goal/graph identity; it contains no
  profile, raw dialog text, Course/path/lesson identity, execution job, or
  content. Its `(student_id,idempotency_key)` and
  `(student_id,state_ref_kind,state_ref_version)` unique constraints are the
  replay and no-double-handoff fences. Migration `009` down fails closed while
  any receipt evidence exists under an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` table lock; row and
  statement triggers protect update/delete/truncate immutability.
  `readiness_observed_at` is the bounded historical observation
  instant and is no later than `created_at`.
- `onboarding_path_execution` is the separate S9 executor, uniquely keyed by
  immutable S8 `handoff_id`. It persists the Student admission ID, current
  monotonic fence and expiry, exact Course-owned lesson bindings, and distinct
  stable operation keys before AI or Course effects; it never changes the S8
  receipt. Every parsed AI lesson response and its deterministic prompt key/hash
  is write-once before the next prompt call, so a crash resumes only missing
  lessons. Snapshot, assembled generated Course and downstream receipts are
  write-once. Update, delete, and truncate guards
  protect execution evidence. Migration `010` down fails closed after any
  execution evidence.
- Migration `004_web_practice_targets` adds the exact versioned HTML/CSS/JavaScript target identities and prerequisite edges used by the first BUILD and BUGFIX practice pilots. They are ordinary learning-domain catalog data, not task-local aliases.
- Migration `005_learning_target_stack` adds the many-to-many stack index used only to bound authoring discovery. Canonical identity remains `(target_type, target_key, target_version)`.
- Migration `008_programming_foundation_graph` idempotently publishes exact
  goal `programming.foundation` version `v1`, graph version
  `programming-foundation-graph-v1`, and its six language-neutral targets. It
  adds no stack-index or transition rows and leaves the existing `go.backend`
  seed unchanged.

- Migration `006_course_plan_learning_path` adds the nullable cross-service path ID, its Student/path request index, and the outbox constraint that permits v1 and v2 during rollout. There is intentionally no PostgreSQL foreign key to Student's database.
- Migration `007_course_plan_path_command_checkpoint` adds the nullable exact-path command checkpoint and its private planned outcome. Historical and new-path-allocation-only rows remain null. Retry and terminal updates retain the checkpoint; terminal updates clear the claim/lease and keep the exact command as bounded audit data.
- Migration `011_diagnostic_assessment_plan` adds the immutable placement-only plan receipt and its exact onboarding/bootstrap binding. It selects only frozen Course assessment references; it stores no answers, mastery, or Student path state.
- Migration `012_diagnostic_assessment_delivery_and_placement` adds two immutable Planner-owned receipts: the exact-plan Student reservation delivery proof and the aggregate-only placement decision. Both bind an existing immutable plan relationally, reject non-canonical JSON/digests, and block updates/deletes. Neither stores attempt state, answers, item correctness, scorer data, mastery, learning paths, progress, or evidence.
- Migration `013_diagnostic_bootstrap_binding_and_receipt` adds append-only, rollout-provisioned exact goal/direction Course bindings and immutable bootstrap idempotency receipts. The latest binding revision wins; an inactive latest revision is an explicit fail-closed tombstone. This migration deliberately seeds no Course IDs.
  Its `binding_digest` is `sha256` of the named `diagnostic-bootstrap-binding.v1` projection: schema, normalized goal/direction, Course UUID, revision, `diagnostic-bootstrap-v1`, active/tombstone state, and microsecond UTC creation time. Thus a tombstone has its own immutable digest; no mutable binding interpretation is trusted.

- Migration `014_course_plan_diagnostic_link` adds the nullable, indexed Planner-local `diagnostic_plan_id` foreign key. It is permitted only for Teacher INITIAL commands and never appears in public Course-plan, Student/Course, path, or event contracts.
- Migration `015_project_authoring_flow` adds the durable path-backed project
  state machine and binds one Student/idempotency key to an exact path UUID,
  version, goal, bounded target/input JSON, path digest, and the immutable
  Student onboarding version plus an authoring-profile digest over only the
  normalized locale and canonical desired stack codes used by TZ. The PII-free
  TZ request is separately digested. Version CAS and an expiring claim serialize work. Confirmation, TZ job
  identity, READY digests, explicit publication request, and Practice revision
  receipt become immutable once written. A partial unique index permits at most one non-FAILED flow for the exact immutable Student/path/path-version/path-digest/profile-version/profile-digest snapshot; `FAILED` rows remain auditable and permit a new retry. No answers, profile/mastery snapshot,
  generated source, private verifier data, Sandbox ID, Practice instance, or
  progress mutation is stored.

Migrations are ordered, additive, and reversible. Production migration execution requires explicit approval and `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`.


Project authoring staging lifecycle: verified TZ READY candidates are submitted through `POST /internal/v1/authoring-jobs/{id}/stage`. Planner validates the exact `practice-task-staging-receipt.v1`, job identity, candidate/blueprint digests and verified artifact digests, then durably records `STAGED` and the immutable receipt. Staging creates no public revision. The existing Planner `/publish` command fails closed for generated, READY and STAGED candidates because Practice-owned acceptance and post-acceptance publication integration are deferred. Historical publication receipts remain readable; staging never writes a publication receipt or PUBLISHED.

Migration `018_project_authoring_staging` adds the immutable staging receipt. Its down migration deliberately fails when STAGED records exist, rolling back atomically to avoid discarding staged evidence. The fresh database runner applies all 18 forward migrations.

Migration `019_course_planning_input_checkpoint` independently adds three private
immutable worker tables: `course_planning_input_checkpoint`,
`course_planning_generated_checkpoint`, and `course_planning_ensure_checkpoint`.
It does not depend on project-authoring migration 018 and backfills no historical
jobs. Rollout requires an explicitly approved manual migration before deploying
workers that assert `PinnedCoursePlanRepository` on the request Store.

The first checkpoint binds request/student/request-hash/goal/intent, exact graph
and policy, normalized bounded historical profile and mastery projections,
diagnostic route and original onboarding/direction fences, original caller path
identity and optional exact path state, deterministic draft, unchanged
student-neutral `course-fingerprint-v1` digest, exact normalized context, and gap
refs. Private `InputHash` may bind Student identity; CourseFingerprint never does.
INITIAL's original caller path stays absent after internal allocation resolves
`course_plan_request.learning_path_id`. A previously resolved, ungenerated
INITIAL can pin that exact observed path state without inventing a caller path.
These projections are historical job inputs; Student remains the source of truth.
A joint atomic Student snapshot or global mastery-version fence is outside this
migration. No raw evidence, answers, secrets, or provider prompts are retained.

Generated Course enrichment is bound to the input hash and unchanged draft
structure. The actual Course ensure receipt and ordered lesson bindings bind
both hashes and are durable before Student effects. The input payload is bounded at 32 MiB to accommodate the existing 16 MiB
generated-draft limit plus historical projections; ensure receipts are bounded
at 1 MiB. These bounds fail explicitly and never truncate planning inputs.
Each checkpoint stores
original `BYTEA` payload bytes plus SHA-256; JSONB key reordering cannot alter
existing fingerprint context or artifact identity. Typed reads verify byte SHA,
self hash, parent hash, request binding, bounds, and original applicability fences.
Unknown fields, partial chains, corrupted pins, and active legacy generated
partials with no trustworthy new input binding fail closed. Read and transient
storage errors propagate separately from malformed-checkpoint validation.

Only a matching unexpired worker claim may insert or identically replay a pin,
serialized by a locked request row. Schema header checks and relational parent
hash guards supplement domain validation. Update, delete, and truncate are
rejected; terminal requests retain all three checkpoints. Migration 019 DOWN
locks all three tables in `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` mode and refuses any retained pin,
including failed or completed jobs. Apply it only after an explicit retention
and migration decision; it is not a checkpoint-discard operation.
